speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: asked the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (a) whether the Ministry will study the impact of the policy on banning single-use plastics in the UK and Ireland; and (b) what is the Ministry's assessment of the likelihood of adopting a similar ban here.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: My Ministry and the National Environment Agency (NEA) take a keen interest in how other countries manage their disposables.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: We will continue to study their policies and implementation outcomes and how they may fit into our local context.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Our approach has been to reduce the excessive use of all types of disposables, not just single-use plastics, and to promote the use of reusables.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: As such, our focus is to promote the use of reusables.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: NEA launched the "Say YES to Waste Less" campaign last month as part of the Year Towards Zero Waste movement to drive awareness of the impact of excessive consumption of disposables and the need for reduction.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Some 1,600 premises, ranging from retailers, food and beverage establishments, supermarkets, hotels, Community Development Councils, grassroots organisations, schools and non-governmental organisations (NGOs) have come forward to partner NEA in this nationwide endeavour.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Partners commit to actions, such as prompting customers to bring along reusables, encouraging them to decline disposable cutlery with online orders and displaying campaign visuals at cashier points.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: NEA has also launched the "Towards Zero Waste Grant" to support individuals, interest groups, NGOs, grassroots organisations and corporations to initiate or scale up waste reduction and recycling initiatives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: This will increase companies’ awareness of the potential for waste reduction in their business operations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Besides reducing waste, we are also taking actions to increase our recycling rate.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Through this initiative, we hope to engage the public to consciously recycle used polyethylene terephthalate (PET) bottles and aluminium cans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: At the same time, we are developing the local recycling industry.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Where possible, we want to better extract resources from waste and close the waste loop domestically.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: NEA is currently studying recycling solutions and technologies and assessing their suitability for adoption in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: This may include mechanical recycling to turn plastic waste into plastic pellets for manufacturing new products, or chemical recycling to turn plastic waste into chemical feedstock or fuel.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: The Government will work with industry stakeholders to explore how these technologies can be applied to Singapore, such that it is both environmentally and economically sustainable.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: These are efforts which could help grow local enterprises and create good jobs for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Everyone needs to play our part to reduce packaging waste, including single-use plastics.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: For example, we can opt out of receiving disposable cutlery when ordering food for takeaway or delivery, or we can bring our own reusable bags and containers and take only the plastic bags we need and use.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: The support of the public, businesses and the community is key to successfully reducing our packaging waste.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: But there is one common topic that I always hear being discussed by my residents, especially when they come back from overseas.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: They say that even Bangkok is charging for the use of plastic bags.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Even Malacca is charging for the use of plastic bags and they were asking why is it that, in Singapore, we are so reluctant to charge for the use of plastic bags.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Perhaps, the Senior Minister of State can share with us.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: First, I must say that, coming from Er Dr Lee Bee Wah, this is pretty good news, commending MEWR for our work as well as giving me feedback that the residents are asking why we are not charging for plastic bags.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As I have said earlier in my reply, we are interested and are closely monitoring developments on this front, such as how other countries are managing their disposables.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We will study their policies and implementation outcome and see how they fit into our local context.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But, currently, instead of just singling out single-use plastics – pardon the pun – we are focusing on reducing the excessive consumption of all types of disposables.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We think this is a more sustainable approach for various reasons.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Therefore, we do not face the challenges faced by many other countries which are more reliant on direct landfilling of their waste.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We also have use, for instance, for single-use plastic bags.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The majority of Singaporeans live in high-rise public housing with the refuse chute and we have worked hard for years to inculcate this habit of bagging your rubbish before you dispose of it, to maintain good public hygiene.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We do not want to undo such efforts.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Irresponsible disposal is going to lead to public hygiene issues like pest infestation, for instance.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, we are actually focusing on reducing all types of disposables and doing it upfront, for instance.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We also have a very comprehensive and integrated waste collection and disposal system, and we have measures in place to address the issue, for instance, of marine litter pollution and micro-plastics, because we have litter traps to trap the waste or litter that may get into the oceans.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We have beach, coastal and underwater clean-ups, and we have flotsam removal craft that we use regularly.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As I have said, we have strengthened our efforts on this front in various ways to the "Say YES to Waste Less" campaign as well as the mandatory reporting and Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) framework in future.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In fact, for the	"Say YES to Waste Less" campaign, what we are really doing is to work with our partners and get our partners to come up with ground-up programmes to discourage the use of disposables and encourage the use of reusables, either by incentivising consumers or charging for single-use plastic bags, as some had done, or not using plastic bags at all.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I also join Er Dr Lee Bee Wah to congratulate MEWR for the good work you are doing, but we are not saying to ban plastic bags or replace plastic bags.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We are calling for the plastic bag charge so that we can reduce the use of plastic bags, so that we do not over-consume it.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If we focus on this, then the "Say YES to Waste Less" campaign will go a lot faster.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The Senior Minister of State mentioned about other countries.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So, it is not about replacing but about reducing.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Not to repeat myself, again, let me say that we are taking into account our own local unique context.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And for the various reasons that I have listed earlier and shared, we are taking the approach of actually not singling out single-use plastics.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Charging for single-use plastic bags will be singling out just plastics.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Therefore, we are looking at how we can reduce excessive consumption of all types of disposables, including plastics, of course.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: A few months back when Mr Louis Ng moved the Adjournment Motion on reducing the use of plastic bags, I thought he made a lot of sense.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I do not see why MEWR is so resistant to imposing charges for plastic bags.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: When I go overseas, and when they tell me, "You have to pay five cents or 10 cents if you want a plastic bag", the general attitude of most consumers is that "I must as well cut on it".

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: That helps to reduce the use of plastic bags.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I would urge MEWR to reconsider the Motion moved by Mr Louis Ng again, because I really think that it will help reduce the use of plastic bags.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, let us look at how these policies and measures will pan out in terms of effectiveness of reducing the amount of disposables.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Firms, supermarkets, retailers and so on can already do this on their own volition, and we will support them.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Our feedback has not been as if it is overwhelmingly that charging for plastic bags is the way to go.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In fact, every time when there is an issue on this, there will always be views from both sides of the camp.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And when we look at this, as I have said, there are actually good reasons that single-use plastic bags have to be given, for instance, or used by the public for bagging their waste and so on.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And therefore, the issue is really about excessive use; not that you cannot use plastic bags but excessive use of plastic bags.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The Senior Minister of State alluded to studies that show that one has to use reusable packaging or reusable bags a certain number of times before you improve on the carbon emissions, vis-a-vis using single-use plastics.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I think such data has been cited also previously.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I believe there is a factsheet online from NEA on the findings of the lifecycle assessment study on carrier bags and food packaging.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I think what we have put up is what is useful to the public, not some of the details.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But obviously, we can share with Members some of the methodologies.
